chapter: New York 1936-39 (second pass of the transcript)
title: Bill Doggett's Philadelphia big band (second pass)
summary: Repeat of the Doggett band and Hall bringing Philadelphians to New York.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Yeah. And prior to that I had been working with Bill Dawgett in Philadelphia and we had a big band, Shadow Wilson was the drummer.
Now, when was this? I mean, you talked about Philadelphia but we didn't --
This was just before I left.
Before you went to the Catskills?
Yeah.
So you and Bill Dawgett had a, who was the leader of the band?
Bill Dawgett. Yeah, we had a big band. We used to work in ballrooms.
This was before he was an organist?
Oh, yeah, yeah, much before, though he used to play --
Shadow was on drums?
Yeah, we used to play saxaphone. Oh, wow. What's that terrific saxaphone player, alto.
You mean in those days?
Any day. He's still --
Benny Carter.

Benny Carter, we used to play all of his tunes, that type of thing. Bill Dawgett was very astute arranger at that period of time and he reached out for tunes to play for the band and so we were playing things that were different from anybody else.
Who were your soloists, do you remember?
It wasn't a solo sort of thing, it was an ensemble. I don't remember all the guys in the band. I can find out who they are.
I was just wondering if there was anyone, who again like yourself, went on to New York.

Well, I left there, I left first out of that period. I left first. Acidentally, you know, then all of the rest of the guys who would come from Philadelphia would come look me up. I was known to get them their first gig in New York.
Yeah, someone from home to say hello to.
